hyps.why: Increasing an already large learning rate causes divergence, while at low rates it speeds up training.
Tiny learning rates undertrain in 243 epochs, so raising them helps substantially.
Larger batches mean fewer updates, which compounds undertraining at a low learning rate.
Small batches add gradient noise that destabilizes training at a high learning rate.
More updates per epoch compensate for a slow learning rate.
Wider networks are less stable at large learning rates, reducing the benefit of width.
Deeper networks diverge more easily with a large learning rate.
Very strong L2 causes underfitting, whereas small alpha has little effect.
Wider networks make faster progress per step, helping when the learning rate is small.
Deeper networks train slowly at tiny learning rates in a fixed epoch budget.
